FUS-01.question: How many tickets were sold in total for all 1. Bundesliga matches in the 2024/25 season?
FUS-01.context: 18 clubs, 34 matchdays, home and away. Counts all tickets sold for the 306 league matches, according to the DFL.
FUS-01.explanation: According to the DFL economic report, exactly 11,653,239 tickets were sold in the 2024/25 Bundesliga season, an average of 38,082 per match at 95.9% capacity.
FUS-01.introduction: First the number of matches, then a typical stadium average.
steps: 18 clubs each play each other twice: 18 × 17 = 306 matches (or 9 matches × 34 matchdays).
Assumption: stadiums hold about 45,000 people on average and are nearly full, so about 40,000 spectators per match.

FUS-02.question: How many hours of pure playing time would you have to watch to see every match of the 2024/25 Bundesliga season in full?
FUS-02.context: Only the regular 90 minutes per match, without stoppage time, half-time or ads.
FUS-02.explanation: A Bundesliga season has 306 matches (18 teams, 34 matchdays). 306 × 90 minutes = 27,540 minutes = 459 hours, a good 19 days without sleep.
FUS-02.introduction: Number of matches times match length, then convert to hours.
steps: Each matchday has 9 matches (18 teams, always two playing each other).
34 matchdays × 9 matches = about 300 matches.
Assumption: 90 minutes = 1.5 hours per match.
300 × 1.5 = 450 hours (about 19 days non-stop).

FUS-03.question: What is the combined pitch area of all 18 Bundesliga stadiums in square metres?
FUS-03.context: Only the pitches within the lines, 2024/25 season. Assumes the standard pitch size set by the DFB.
FUS-03.explanation: The DFB set 105 × 68 metres as the standard size, which is 7,140 m² per pitch. 18 stadiums × 7,140 m² = 128,520 m², about 12.9 hectares – roughly 18 soccer pitches or about 1,000 single-family house plots.
FUS-03.introduction: A pitch is roughly 100 by 70 metres – and there are 18 of them.
steps: Assumption: a professional pitch measures about 100 × 70 metres.
100 × 70 = 7,000 m² per pitch.

FUS-04.question: How many kilometres did all outfield players run in total across the 64 matches of the 2022 World Cup in Qatar?
FUS-04.context: Counts the running distance of both teams in all 64 matches, normalised to 90 minutes (excluding goalkeepers and extra time), according to FIFA analysis.
FUS-04.explanation: According to the FIFA Training Centre, a team at the 2022 World Cup ran an average of 108.1 km per match (normalised to 90 minutes, excluding goalkeepers). 108.1 km × 2 teams × 64 matches = 13,837 km, so about 13,800 km – roughly a third of the way around the Earth.
FUS-04.introduction: About 10 km per player per match is a well-known rule of thumb.
steps: Assumption: an outfield player runs about 10 km per match.
10 outfield players × 10 km = 100 km per team per match.
Two teams: 200 km per match.
A World Cup has 64 matches: 64 × 200 = 12,800 km.

FUS-05.question: How many litres of beer are served at Signal Iduna Park in Dortmund during a Borussia Dortmund home match?
FUS-05.context: Germany's largest stadium with 81,365 seats. Figure from the BVB stadium documentary for the 2025/26 season, given by the head of spectator catering.
FUS-05.explanation: According to BVB catering chief Merlin Zepter, between 60,000 and 62,500 litres of beer flow per home match – a good 120,000 half-litre cups, or about three quarters of a litre per spectator.
FUS-05.introduction: Spectators times share of beer drinkers times cups per head.
steps: The stadium is usually full: about 80,000 spectators.
Assumption: about half drink beer, so 40,000 people.
Assumption: on average 2 cups of 0.5 litres per drinker = 1 litre.
40,000 × 1 litre = 40,000 litres.

FUS-06.question: How many million pounds did the 20 Premier League clubs spend on players in total during the 2023 summer transfer window?
FUS-06.context: Gross transfer spending of all 20 clubs in the 2023 summer window (June to 1 September), according to the Deloitte Sports Business Group.
FUS-06.explanation: According to Deloitte, Premier League clubs spent a record £2.36 billion (£2,355 million) in summer 2023 – almost £440 million more than the previous record of £1.92 billion in summer 2022.
FUS-06.introduction: Clubs times new signings times typical fee.
steps: Assumption: each of the 20 clubs signs about 5 players for a fee in the summer.
20 × 5 = 100 transfers.
Assumption: an average Premier League transfer costs about £20 million (a few for 80+, many for under 10).
100 × £20 million = £2,000 million.

FUS-07.question: How many kilograms does the original FIFA World Cup Trophy weigh, the one the world champions lift after the final?
FUS-07.context: The trophy designed by Silvio Gazzaniga and used since 1974, 36.8 cm tall, made of 18-carat gold with a malachite base.
FUS-07.explanation: According to FIFA, the trophy weighs exactly 6.175 kg and is 36.8 cm tall. It is hollow inside – if it were solid gold, it would weigh around 70 to 80 kg.
FUS-07.introduction: The trophy is about as tall as a large water bottle, but hollow.
steps: Assumption: the trophy has roughly the volume of a 1.5-litre bottle, so 1,500 cm³.
Assumption: only about 15% of that is actually metal (the walls), so about 225 cm³.
Gold weighs about 19 g/cm³: 225 × 19 ≈ 4,300 g.
Plus a stone base of about 1 kg: about 5.3 kg.

FUS-08.question: How many soccer matches in Germany were officiated by referees in total in the 2024/25 season – from the Bundesliga down to the lowest district leagues?
FUS-08.context: All officially scheduled matches under the DFB umbrella with its roughly 140,000 registered teams (incl. youth, women and amateurs).
FUS-08.explanation: According to the DFB 2024/25 membership statistics, the more than 60,000 active referees officiated just under 1.4 million matches – about 3,800 matches per day.
FUS-08.introduction: Start from the number of teams, then matches per team per season.
steps: Germany has about 140,000 registered teams.
Assumption: each team plays about 20 competitive matches per season.
140,000 × 20 = 2,800,000 team appearances.
Every match involves two teams: 2,800,000 / 2 = 1,400,000 matches.
Not every match has an official referee (children's soccer): about 1,200,000.

FUS-09.question: How many official "Al Rihla" match balls did the two manufacturers produce for FIFA for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar?
FUS-09.context: Only the match balls delivered to FIFA (for matches, team training, associations and tournament operations) – not the millions of balls for retail sale.
FUS-09.explanation: According to Hassan Masood, director of Pakistani manufacturer Forward Sports, the two producers (Pakistan and China) together delivered about 300,000 match balls to FIFA; including retail versions for the open market, there were about 10 million Al Rihla balls.
FUS-09.introduction: The 64 matches themselves only need a few thousand balls – the lion's share goes to teams, associations and tournament operations.
steps: Matches: 64 × about 20 balls = about 1,300 balls.
Assumption: each of the 32 teams gets about 1,000 balls for preparation and training = 32,000.
Assumption: all 211 FIFA member associations receive about 500 balls each for coaching and youth = about 105,000.
Assumption: referees, fan festivals, sponsors, media and reserves another 100,000 or so.
Total: about 240,000 balls.

FUS-10.question: According to FIFA, how many people worldwide watched the 2022 World Cup final between Argentina and France on screen?
FUS-10.context: Global reach of the final on 18 December 2022 (TV and streaming), as announced by FIFA one month after the tournament.
FUS-10.explanation: FIFA reported "almost 1.5 billion" viewers for the final; across the whole tournament, about 5 billion people are said to have engaged with the World Cup. There were 88,966 fans in the stadium in Lusail.
FUS-10.introduction: Break it down from the world population.
steps: The world has about 8 billion people.
Assumption: about half have access to TV/internet and are generally interested in soccer: 4 billion.
Assumption: about a third of them actually watch the final (time zone, daily life, no interest in the match).
4 billion / 3 ≈ 1.3 billion viewers.

EIS-01.question: How heavy is the Stanley Cup, the trophy awarded to the NHL champion?
EIS-01.context: The players lift the trophy over their heads after winning the Final. It is made of a silver-nickel alloy and is about 90 cm tall.
EIS-01.referencePeriod: Current version of the trophy (Hockey Hall of Fame figure)
EIS-01.explanation: The Hockey Hall of Fame gives the Stanley Cup's weight as 34.5 lbs or 15.56 kg and its height as 89.54 cm.
EIS-01.introduction: The trophy is almost a metre tall and made of metal – but hollow inside. How heavy does that make it?
steps: Assumption: the trophy is about 90 cm tall, and the base (barrel) is about 45 cm in diameter.
Assumption: the metal walls are only a few millimetres thick; most of it is hollow.
Comparison: a full 10-litre bucket of water weighs 10 kg – a player should easily be able to lift that over his head.
A solid metal trophy of this size would be well over 100 kg; hollow with thin walls, you end up at roughly 10–20 kg.

EIS-02.question: How many people (players, coaches, staff) were engraved on the trophy itself after the 2025 Stanley Cup Final?
EIS-02.context: Each championship team may have its names engraved on one of the five rings on the base (2024/25: Florida Panthers with 52 names). When a ring is full, the oldest one is removed and displayed at the Hockey Hall of Fame. Only the names on the trophy itself count, not the retired rings.
EIS-02.referencePeriod: After the 2025 Stanley Cup Final (latest engraving: Florida Panthers 2024/25)
EIS-02.explanation: The Hockey Hall of Fame counts 2,603 people engraved on the trophy (latest entry: Florida Panthers 2024/25); including the retired rings, there are 3,489. A maximum of 52 names may be engraved per championship team.
EIS-02.introduction: The trophy bears the names of the championship teams of recent decades – how many people does that add up to?
steps: Assumption: five rings on the base, each holding about 13 championship teams – so about 65 teams on the trophy.
Assumption: each championship team has about 20 players plus 10–15 coaches and staff engraved, so about 35 names.
65 teams × 35 names ≈ 2,300 names.
Plus a few old names in the bowl and on the collar – roughly 2,500.

EIS-03.question: How many registered female ice hockey players (women and girls) were there worldwide in 2022 across IIHF member associations?
EIS-03.context: The world governing body IIHF records the licensed players of its member associations every year. Women's hockey is growing strongly: between 2017 and 2022, the number of female players rose by 16%.
EIS-03.explanation: According to the IIHF, the number of registered female players rose from 193,810 (2017) to 225,429 (2022) – an average of about 4,900 per member association.
EIS-03.introduction: Women's hockey is heavily concentrated in North America – that's where the estimate starts.
steps: Assumption: Canada has about 100,000 registered female players, the USA about 90,000.
Assumption: the strong European countries (Sweden, Finland, Czechia, Switzerland, etc.) add up to about 40,000.
Assumption: all other countries combined roughly 10,000.

EIS-04.question: How many spectators attended the regular season of the Swiss National League in 2023/24 in total?
EIS-04.context: 14 teams played a total of 364 regular-season games over 52 rounds (excluding playoffs). The league reported a record attendance.
EIS-04.explanation: SRF reported a record average of 7,130 spectators per game across 364 regular-season games: 7,130 × 364 ≈ 2,595,000, just under 2.6 million – as also stated in the article.
EIS-04.introduction: The Swiss league is surprisingly well attended for its size. Let's multiply games by average.
steps: Assumption: 14 teams, each playing 52 regular-season games → 14 × 52 ÷ 2 = 364 games.
Assumption: Bern draws about 15,000, small arenas like Ajoie or Rapperswil more like 4,000–5,000. An average of about 6,500 seems plausible.
364 × 6,500 ≈ 2.4 million spectators.

EIS-05.question: How many litres of water does it take to build the ice surface of an NHL arena once from scratch?
EIS-05.context: An NHL ice surface measures 200 × 85 feet (about 61 × 26 metres). The ice is sprayed on in many thin layers and ends up only about 2.5 cm (1 inch) thick.
EIS-05.referencePeriod: Standard NHL ice surface (200 × 85 feet, approx. 1 inch thick)
EIS-05.explanation: According to PBS North Carolina, an NHL ice surface needs about 10,600 US gallons of water; 10,600 × 3.785 litres ≈ 40,000 litres. That's about 40 cubic metres.
EIS-05.introduction: Area times thickness gives the volume – and a cubic metre of water is 1,000 litres.
steps: Assumption: the ice surface is about 60 m × 26 m ≈ 1,560 m² (ignoring the rounded corners).
Assumption: the ice is about 2.5 cm = 0.025 m thick.
Volume: 1,560 m² × 0.025 m ≈ 39 m³.
39 m³ × 1,000 litres/m³ ≈ 39,000 litres.

EIS-06.question: How many hockey sticks do all NHL teams go through combined in one season?
EIS-06.context: Pros constantly break, wear out or swap their carbon sticks. In the 2019/20 season, the NHL had 31 teams. A Detroit Red Wings equipment manager estimated usage at 70 to 120 sticks per player per year.
EIS-06.explanation: According to the Associated Press (February 2020), a full team goes through about 1,600 sticks per season, over 50,000 league-wide. Jack Eichel alone used about 100 per season.
EIS-06.introduction: Sticks are consumables – a pro always has a dozen new ones ready.
steps: Assumption: an NHL player uses about 2 sticks per week, so roughly 70 sticks over an 8-month season.
Assumption: a team has about 25 players on the roster (incl. reserves and goalies).
25 × 70 ≈ 1,750 sticks per team.
31 teams × 1,750 ≈ 54,000 sticks.

EIS-07.question: How many kilometres does a Zamboni ice resurfacer travel per year in a typical ice rink?
EIS-07.context: When resurfacing, a Zamboni drives in lanes over the entire ice surface at only about 15 km/h. In a busy rink, the ice is resurfaced about ten times a day. The question asks for the distance per machine per year according to the manufacturer.
EIS-07.referencePeriod: Zamboni Company figure (typical use per year)
EIS-07.explanation: Zamboni states that a machine travels about 3/4 of a mile per resurfacing and covers 'close to 2,000 miles' per year; 2,000 miles × 1.609 ≈ 3,200 km.
EIS-07.introduction: An ice surface is covered in lanes – that adds up over a day, and even more over a year.
steps: Assumption: the ice surface is about 60 m long; the machine is about 2 m wide and, with overlap, drives about 15 lanes.
15 lanes × 60 m ≈ 900 m, plus turns and edges: about 1.2 km per resurfacing.
Assumption: about 8 resurfacings per day on about 300 operating days → 2,400 runs per year.
2,400 × 1.2 km ≈ 2,900 km per year.

EIS-08.question: How many kilometres did the Winnipeg Jets fly during the 2024/25 NHL regular season?
EIS-08.context: Winnipeg is in the middle of Canada; the 41 road games take the team from Vancouver to Florida. The question asks for the team's flight distance over the 82 regular-season games (analysis by TJ Stats, published by The Hockey News).
EIS-08.explanation: Based on a schedule analysis by Thomas Nestico (TJ Stats), The Hockey News reported about 48,200 miles for the Jets, 'nearly 78,000 km' – 6th in the league. The minimum was Pittsburgh with approx. 31,700 miles (approx. 51,000 km).
EIS-08.introduction: 41 road games, often on multi-game trips – we estimate the average distance per road game.
steps: Assumption: 41 road games per season; outbound and return flight for each trip.
Assumption: Winnipeg–Toronto is about 1,500 km, Winnipeg–Los Angeles about 2,500 km. We estimate an average of 1,800 km per one-way leg.
Assumption: thanks to multi-game trips, it's not 82 single flights but roughly 45 flight legs.

EIS-09.question: Roughly how many pucks are used in games during an NHL regular season (2023/24)?
EIS-09.context: Pucks are frozen so they don't bounce. If a puck has been in play for more than a few minutes or flies into the crowd, a fresh one comes out of the cooler. The NHL says 40 to 45 different pucks are typically used per game. 1,312 games were played in 2023/24.
EIS-09.explanation: With about 42 pucks per game (NHL figure: 40–45) and 1,312 games, that gives 42 × 1,312 ≈ 55,000 pucks – excluding playoffs and practices.
EIS-09.introduction: Pucks are disposable: a new one every few minutes, plus the ones that fly into the stands.
steps: 32 teams × 82 games ÷ 2 = 1,312 games.
Assumption: 60 minutes of playing time, a fresh puck about every 2 minutes → about 30 pucks per game.
Assumption: plus about 10 pucks that fly into the crowd or over the boards → about 40 per game.

EIS-10.question: How many Zamboni ice resurfacers has the Zamboni Company delivered in total since its founding in 1949 up to 2025?
EIS-10.context: Frank Zamboni built the first ice resurfacing machine in 1949. The California company still builds every machine by hand and supplies ice rinks all over the world. The question asks for the total number of machines ever delivered, according to the manufacturer.
EIS-10.referencePeriod: Manufacturer figure, as of 2025 (over 75 years since 1949)
EIS-10.explanation: The Zamboni Company states on its website that over 14,000 Zamboni machines have been delivered worldwide (an older FAQ figure still said more than 12,000).
EIS-10.introduction: A niche company that has been building machines by hand for over 75 years – how many does that add up to?
steps: Assumption: there are roughly 10,000 ice rinks worldwide, most with one or two resurfacers – not all of them Zambonis.
Assumption: a machine lasts about 20 years; over 75 years many rinks were re-equipped three or four times, but there were far fewer rinks in the early decades.
Assumption: averaged over the 75 years, about 150 machines delivered per year.
75 years × 150 ≈ 11,000 machines.

BSK-01.question: How many evenings would it take to watch every game of the 2023/24 NBA regular season individually – one game per evening?
BSK-01.context: 30 teams, each playing 82 games. The question is the number of regular-season games (excluding playoffs), i.e. the number of evenings.
BSK-01.explanation: The 2023/24 NBA regular season had 1,230 games. One game per evening means 1,230 evenings – a good three years and four months for a single season.
BSK-01.introduction: Every game involves two teams – forget that and you end up with double the answer.
steps: Assumption: 30 teams in the league.
Assumption: each team plays around 80 games per season.
30 × 80 = 2,400 team appearances.
Each game has 2 teams on the court: 2,400 ÷ 2 = 1,200 games.
One game per evening → around 1,200 evenings.

BSK-02.question: How many free throws were attempted in the entire 2023/24 NBA regular season (made or missed)?
BSK-02.context: Counts all free-throw attempts by all 30 teams across the whole regular season (1,230 games, excluding playoffs).
BSK-02.explanation: In 2023/24 the league-average team attempted 1,781 free throws per season (21.7 per game, 17.0 of them made). 30 teams × 1,781 = 53,430, so around 53,400 free-throw attempts – Orlando led the way with 2,002.
BSK-02.introduction: Every shooting foul brings two free throws – and in the NBA, players foul constantly.
steps: Assumption: around 1,200 games in the regular season.
Assumption: each team attempts about 20 free throws per game (approx. 10 fouls with free throws × 2).
Both teams per game: 2 × 20 = 40 free throws.
Result: around 48,000 free-throw attempts.

BSK-03.question: How many kilometres do all 30 NBA teams combined travel to their games in the 2025/26 regular season?
BSK-03.context: This means the sum of all 30 teams' travel distances from venue to venue over the whole regular season (based on the schedule, straight-line distance between cities).
BSK-03.explanation: The travel distances of all 30 teams (calculated by analyst Chris Gunther, published via Bleacher Report) add up to 1,285,372 miles = around 2.07 million kilometres; the Orlando Magic travel the most with 53,131 miles, the Indiana Pacers the least with 35,267 miles. Calculation: 1,285,372 × 1.609 km ≈ 2,068,600 km.
BSK-03.introduction: The USA is huge – and every team flies to 41 away games.
steps: Assumption: each team has around 40 away games, plus the flights home → about 45 flights per season.
Assumption: an average flight is around 1,500 km (some short hops like Boston–New York, some transcontinental flights over 4,000 km).
45 × 1,500 km = 67,500 km per team.
Result: around 2 million kilometres.

BSK-04.question: What is the combined playing area of all 30 NBA courts in square metres?
BSK-04.context: Only the actual court inside the lines counts (no run-off areas, benches, etc.), one court for each of the 30 teams. NBA courts have the same dimensions everywhere.
BSK-04.referencePeriod: NBA (30 teams), standard court size 94 × 50 feet
BSK-04.explanation: An NBA court measures 94 × 50 feet = 28.65 × 15.24 m = around 437 m². Times 30 courts: 437 × 30 ≈ 13,100 m² – about 1.3 hectares of hardwood, less than two soccer fields.
BSK-04.introduction: A basketball court is smaller than you think – roughly as long as a 25 m swimming pool plus a bit.
steps: Assumption: a court is around 28 m long and 15 m wide.
28 × 15 = 420 m² per court.
Result: around 12,600 square metres.

BSK-05.question: How many three-pointers were made in the entire 2023/24 NBA regular season?
BSK-05.context: Counts all made threes by all 30 teams across the whole regular season (excluding playoffs).
BSK-05.explanation: In 2023/24 the league-average team made 1,053 threes per season (12.8 per game on 35.1 attempts). 30 teams × 1,053 = 31,590, so around 31,600 made threes.
BSK-05.introduction: Threes are routine now: a team attempts over 30 per game and makes a good one in three.
steps: Assumption: around 1,200 games in the regular season.
Assumption: each team makes about 12 threes per game.
Both teams per game: 2 × 12 = 24 threes.
Result: just under 29,000 threes.

BSK-06.question: How many pairs of basketball shoes does NBA star Cade Cunningham say he goes through in a single season?
BSK-06.context: Cunningham (Detroit Pistons) is one of the players who switch to fresh shoes very often. The question is the number per season he gave himself (as of spring 2026).
BSK-06.explanation: Cade Cunningham and Josh Giddey both say they go through around 60 pairs per season. According to the report, most NBA players get by with about 10 pairs – Jarrett Allen even wore his pair for around a year and a half.
BSK-06.introduction: 82 games plus practices – and for sneakerheads, almost every game means a shoe change.
steps: Assumption: around 80 regular-season games, plus playoffs and practices.
Assumption: a frequent switcher takes a new pair roughly every second game → 80 ÷ 2 = 40 pairs.
Plus a few pairs for practices and specials (All-Star, playoffs): + approx. 10 pairs.
Result: around 50 pairs per season.

BSK-07.question: How much did all 30 NBA teams pay in player salaries combined in the 2023/24 season – in millions of USD?
BSK-07.context: This means the sum of all team payrolls (player salaries) of the 30 NBA teams in the 2023/24 season. The salary cap that season was USD 136 million per team, but almost every team exceeded it.
BSK-07.explanation: The payrolls of all 30 teams added up to around USD 5.07 billion in 2023/24 (an average of just under 169 million per team; Golden State at the top with approx. 225 million, Utah at the bottom with approx. 132 million).
BSK-07.introduction: In the NBA the salary cap is more of a soft limit – most teams are above it.
steps: Assumption: 2023/24 salary cap around USD 136 million per team.
Assumption: most teams are 10–40% over the cap → typical payroll about USD 165 million.
30 teams × 165 million = USD 4,950 million.
Result: around USD 5 billion, i.e. approx. 5,000 million.

BSK-08.question: How many players on NBA rosters at the start of the 2023/24 season were not from the USA?
BSK-08.context: Counts all international players (born outside the USA) on the rosters of all 30 teams on opening night of the 2023/24 season. The NBA reported a record figure.
BSK-08.explanation: According to the NBA, 125 international players from 40 countries and territories were on rosters at the start of the 2023/24 season – a record. The largest contingents: Canada (26), France (14), Australia (9), Serbia (7), Germany (6).
BSK-08.introduction: First the roster size, then the share of foreign players – which is now surprisingly high in the NBA.
steps: Assumption: 30 teams with around 15 players each → 30 × 15 = 450 players.
Assumption: roughly one in four players is not from the USA (Canada, France, Australia, the Balkans ...).
Result: around 110 international players.

BSK-09.question: How many spectators attended the games of the 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup in the Philippines, Japan and Indonesia in total?
BSK-09.context: The 2023 World Cup took place from 25 August to 10 September 2023 with 32 teams in five arenas. The question is the total number of arena spectators over the whole tournament.
BSK-09.explanation: According to FIBA, more than 700,665 fans attended the 2023 World Cup games. The record crowd was the opening game Philippines vs Dominican Republic with 38,115 spectators at the Philippine Arena.
BSK-09.introduction: 32 teams, just over two weeks, five arenas – how many games, and how full?
steps: Assumption: 32 teams in 8 groups of four → 8 × 6 = 48 group games; with a second group phase, classification games and the knockout round, around 90 games in total.
Assumption: arenas with 10,000 to 15,000 seats, an average of about 7,000 spectators per game (early-round games of small nations are poorly attended, host games are full).
Result: around 630,000 spectators.

BSK-10.question: How many games did an NBA referee officiate on average in the 2023/24 regular season?
BSK-10.context: Every NBA game has three referees on the court (crew chief, referee, umpire). The league's referee staff that season comprised 80 people, who shared all 1,230 games between them.
BSK-10.explanation: 1,230 games × 3 referees on the court = 3,690 assignments, spread over 80 referees → 3,690 ÷ 80 ≈ 46 games per person. The busiest worked 65–66 games, newcomers and part-timers fewer than 10.
BSK-10.introduction: Three people per game, a pool of referees – just count the assignments and divide them up.
steps: Assumption: around 1,200 games in the regular season.
3 referees on the court per game: 1,200 × 3 = 3,600 assignments.
Assumption: the NBA employs about 75 referees.
Result: around 48 games per referee.

AMF-01.question: How many footballs does Wilson make per year at its factory in Ada, Ohio?
AMF-01.context: Since 1941, every NFL point has been scored with a Wilson ball. All official NFL balls are handmade in the small town of Ada, Ohio – but the factory also supplies the college, high-school and fan markets. As of 2024.
AMF-01.explanation: According to Wilson and the NFL (opening of the new factory, June 2024), around 700,000 footballs are made in Ada every year, by about 150 employees in around 20 production steps.
AMF-01.introduction: A craft factory with a limited workforce – estimate via working days and daily output.
steps: Assumption: around 150 people work at the factory.
Assumption: each person produces a net of about 20 finished balls per day (many hands per ball, but all working in parallel).
150 × 20 = 3,000 balls per day.
Assumption: 250 working days per year → 3,000 × 250 = 750,000.

AMF-02.question: How many chicken wings do Americans eat on Super Bowl Sunday 2025 (Super Bowl LIX)?
AMF-02.context: The Super Bowl is the biggest snacking day of the year in the USA. The poultry producers' association (National Chicken Council) publishes a forecast every year for the weekend of the final.
AMF-02.explanation: In its annual Wing Report, the National Chicken Council forecast 1.47 billion wings for Super Bowl LIX – laid end to end, they would circle the Earth more than three times.
AMF-02.introduction: Scale up from the US population via the share of wing eaters.
steps: Assumption: the USA has around 340 million inhabitants.
Assumption: about a third eat wings on Super Bowl Sunday → around 110 million people.
Assumption: about 12 wings per person (a typical plate).
110 million × 12 ≈ 1.3 billion wings.

AMF-03.question: How many kilometres did all NFL offences gain combined through passing in the 2024 regular season?
AMF-03.context: The 2024 regular season comprised 272 games (32 teams with 17 games each). Counts the passing yards of all 32 teams (excluding playoffs), converted into kilometres (1 yard = 0.9144 m).
AMF-03.explanation: Pro Football Reference lists 118,384 passing yards league-wide for 2024. 118,384 × 0.9144 m ≈ 108,250 m, so around 108 km – roughly the distance from Zurich to Bern, thrown in one season.
AMF-03.introduction: A typical NFL team throws for a good 200 yards per game – multiply across the league and convert.
steps: Assumption: a team gains around 220 passing yards per game.
32 teams × 17 games = 544 team games → 544 × 220 ≈ 120,000 yards.
That is around 108 km.

AMF-04.question: How much does a 30-second commercial cost during the TV broadcast of Super Bowl LX (February 2026) on NBC?
AMF-04.context: The Super Bowl is the most-watched TV broadcast in the USA; Super Bowl LIX (2025) drew an average of 127.7 million viewers. Ad slots are sold months in advance. The question is the reported list price in USD.
AMF-04.explanation: According to Adweek (cited by EMARKETER), NBCUniversal charged around USD 8 million per 30-second spot for Super Bowl LX – about 267,000 dollars per second.
AMF-04.introduction: Ad prices scale with reach: work with a price per 1,000 viewers (CPM).
steps: Assumption: around 125 million people watch the Super Bowl.

AMF-09.question: How many offensive plays (passes, runs and sacks) were run in the entire 2024 NFL regular season?

MOT-01.question: How many times does a rear tyre of a Formula 1 car turn during the 2024 Bahrain Grand Prix (full race distance, ignoring pit stops)?
MOT-01.context: The Bahrain International Circuit is 5.412 km long and the race runs over 57 laps. The 18-inch Pirelli tyres have an outer diameter of 720 mm.

steps: Assumption: an F1 race is about 300 km long, i.e. 300,000 m.

Around 135,000 revolutions – per tyre, in just 1.5 hours.

MOT-02.question: How many individual tyres did Pirelli supply in total in the 2024 Formula 1 season (all sets, including those never used)?

Around 38,000 tyres – a large share of them go back to the warehouse unused.

MOT-04.question: How many spectators attended the 2024 British Grand Prix weekend at Silverstone in total (Friday to Sunday, daily attendance added up)?

MOT-05.question: How many kilometres did the winning car of the 2025 24 Hours of Le Mans (Ferrari 499P #83) cover in the 24 hours?

Around 5,000 km.
